claim: Primary cultures of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) express 220 kDa AnkB.
source: We selected primary cultures of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) because these cells express 220 kDa AnkB (Figure 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, which displays an immunoblot demonstrating the presence of 220 kDa AnkB in WT MEFs.

claim: A subset of WT AnkB-mCherry-associated organelles exhibited fast long-range motility with a net velocity greater than 4 µm/s and a persistence greater than 0.5.
source: We observed that a subset of WT AnkB-mCherry-associated organelles exhibited fast long-range motility, with a net velocity greater than 4 µm/s and a persistence greater than 0.5, which is consistent with long-range, fast microtubule-based transport (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from tracking vesicles expressing WT AnkB-mCherry in Ank2-/- MEFs, with quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: DD1320AA AnkB-mCherry-positive organelles showed shorter-range motility, reduced net velocity (velocity < 4 µm/s, persistence < 0.5), and completely lacked a population with fast long-range motion.
source: DD1320AA AnkB-mCherry-positive organelles showed shorter-range motility, reduced net velocity (velocity < 4 µm/s, persistence < 0.5), and completely lacked a population with fast long-range motion (velocity > 4 µm/s, persistence > 0.5), which is otherwise observed in Ank2-/- MEFs expressing WT AnkB-mCherry (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing DD1320AA AnkB-mCherry mutant to WT AnkB-mCherry, shown in Figure 1B and supplementary figure.

claim: AnkB provides long-range motility to a subset of organelles by coupling them through dynactin to either dynein or kinesin motors.
source: Hence, these results demonstrate that AnkB provides long-range motility to a subset of organelles by coupling them through dynactin to either dynein or kinesin motors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing that mutation of the dynactin-binding site (DD1320AA) abolishes long-range motility of AnkB-positive organelles.

claim: Over 70% of WT AnkB-mCherry-positive vesicles detected were PI3P-positive.
source: Live microscopy revealed that over 70% of WT AnkB-mCherry-positive vesicles detected were PI3P-positive, and around 45% of PI3P-positive organelles were associated with WT AnkB-mCherry (Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from live microscopy experiments using GFP-2xFYVE to label PI3P lipids, shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Around 45% of PI3P-positive organelles were associated with WT AnkB-mCherry.
source: Live microscopy revealed that over 70% of WT AnkB-mCherry-positive vesicles detected were PI3P-positive, and around 45% of PI3P-positive organelles were associated with WT AnkB-mCherry (Figure 1D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from live microscopy experiments, shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Mutant R1194A AnkB-mCherry, which cannot bind PI3P lipids, failed to localize to PI3P-positive organelles and was instead diffusely distributed throughout the cytoplasm.
source: In sharp contrast, mutant R1194A AnkB-mCherry, which cannot bind PI3P lipids (Lorenzo et al., 2014) (Figure 1C red circle), failed to localize to PI3P-positive organelles, and was instead diffusely distributed throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing the localization pattern of R1194A AnkB-mCherry mutant compared to WT, with citation to previous work establishing the PI3P-binding deficiency.

claim: WT AnkB-mCherry expressed was preferentially localized to Rab5-positive early endosomes.
source: Although WT AnkB-mCherry expressed was preferentially localized to Rab5-positive early endosomes, it also exhibited partial overlap with Rab11-positive recycling endosomes and LAMP1-positive lysosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization experiments with organelle markers in live MEFs, as referenced in Figure 1F and supplementary figures.

claim: WT AnkB-mCherry exhibited partial overlap with Rab11-positive recycling endosomes and LAMP1-positive lysosomes.
source: Although WT AnkB-mCherry expressed was preferentially localized to Rab5-positive early endosomes, it also exhibited partial overlap with Rab11-positive recycling endosomes and LAMP1-positive lysosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization experiments with organelle markers in live MEFs.

claim: A restricted association of AnkB-mCherry with puncta at mitochondria ends was detected.
source: Moreover, we detected a restricted association of AnkB-mCherry with puncta at mitochondria ends.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations of AnkB-mCherry localization with mitochondrial markers.

claim: Almost no localization of AnkB-mCherry to either Golgi or ER membranes was observed.
source: In contrast, we observed almost no localization of AnkB-mCherry to either Golgi or ER membranes (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization experiments with Golgi and ER markers showing minimal overlap.

claim: PI3P lipids were enriched in endo-lysosomal membranes.
source: As expected (Gillooly et al., 2000; Di Paolo and De Camilli, 2006), PI3P lipids were enriched in endo-lysosomal membranes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using GFP-2xFYVE probe in fixed MEFs, with citations to previous literature establishing this distribution pattern.

claim: AnkB associates with multiple organelles through PI3P lipids and promotes their long-range transport through interaction with the dynactin motor protein adaptor complex.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that AnkB associates with multiple organelles through PI3P lipids and promotes their long-range transport through interaction with the dynactin motor protein adaptor complex.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results showing PI3P-dependent localization and dynactin-dependent motility.

claim: A yeast-two-hybrid screen using the death domain of human AnkB identified ten individual positive clones, all sharing the last 65 C-terminal residues of RabGAP1L.
source: Interestingly, a yeast-two-hybrid (Y2H) screen using the death domain of human AnkB (AnkB DD) (Figure 2A) and a normalized universal mouse cDNA library identified ten individual positive clones, all sharing the last 65 C-terminal residues of RabGAP1L (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from a yeast-two-hybrid screen.

claim: RabGAP1L belongs to the Tre2–Bub2–Cdc16 (TBC) domain-containing family of Rab-specific GTPase-activating proteins.
source: RabGAP1L belongs to the Tre2–Bub2–Cdc16 (TBC) domain-containing family of Rab-specific GTPase-activating proteins (TBC/RabGAPs) (Fukuda, 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature classifying RabGAP1L.

claim: RabGAP1L, via a catalytic site on the TBC domain, inactivates Rab22A by promoting its GDP-bound configuration.
source: Specifically, RabGAP1L, via a catalytic site on the TBC domain, inactivates Rab22A by promoting its GDP-bound configuration (Itoh et al., 2006; Frasa et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature establishing RabGAP1L's enzymatic activity on Rab22A.

claim: Endogenous AnkB and RabGAP1L interact in cells.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) and co-localization experiments using affinity-purified antibodies against AnkB and RabGAP1L, which recognize single polypeptides of 220 kDa and 93 kDa in MEFs, respectively (Figure 1A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), showed that endogenous AnkB and RabGAP1L interact in cells (Figure 2C top).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments using endogenous proteins from MEF lysates.

claim: The AnkG death domain did not interact with RabGAP1L in Y2H assays.
source: Interestingly, the AnkG death domain (AnkG DD), which is 65% homologous with the AnkB DD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), did not interact with RabGAP1L in Y2H assays (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by negative results from yeast-two-hybrid assays.

claim: Full-length endogenous AnkG did not co-immunoprecipitate with RabGAP1L from MEF lysates.
source: Similarly, full-length endogenous AnkG did not co-immunoprecipitate with RabGAP1L from MEF lysates (Figure 2C bottom).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing no interaction between AnkG and RabGAP1L.

claim: Strong PLA labeling of cytoplasmic organelles was observed in WT MEFs and complete loss of signal in Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: Consistent with the Y2H and co-IP results, we observed strong PLA labeling of cytoplasmic organelles in WT MEFs and complete loss of signal in Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: The E1537A substitution significantly weakened the interaction with RabGAP1L, while the reverse-charge mutant E1537K blocked their association.
source: Binding assays between RabGAP1L and AnkB with alanine mutations in seven of its DD charged residues diverging from AnkG's DD (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, red box) showed that the E1537A substitution significantly weakened the interaction with RabGAP1L, while the reverse-charge mutant E1537K blocked their association (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by binding assays testing various mutations in the AnkB death domain.

claim: Reversing the charge of the surface exposed 783KK residues to EE abolishes RabGAP1L binding to AnkB DD in Y2H assays.
source: We found that reversing the charge of the surface exposed 783KK residues to EE (Figure 2G) abolishes RabGAP1L binding to AnkB DD in Y2H assays (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast-two-hybrid assay results testing the KK783EE mutation.

claim: AnkB co-transports with RabGAP1L on motile vesicles.
source: Time-lapse video microscopy assessing the dynamic localization of AnkB-mCherry and RabGAP1L-GFP co-expressed in Ank2-/- MEFs revealed that AnkB co-transports with RabGAP1L. Kymograph analysis confirmed that both proteins were co-localized and co-transported on motile vesicles (Figure 2F top, 2 hr and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse video microscopy and kymograph analysis showing co-transport of AnkB and RabGAP1L.

claim: E1537K AnkB-mCherry, which does not bind RabGAP1L, still localizes to vesicles, but no longer co-transports with RabGAP1L-GFP.
source: In contrast, E1537K AnkB-mCherry, which does not bind RabGAP1L, still localizes to vesicles, but no longer co-transports with RabGAP1L-GFP (Figure 2F bottom, 2 hr and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse video microscopy showing that the E1537K mutation disrupts co-transport while maintaining vesicular localization.

claim: The KK783EE RabGAP1L-GFP mutant that abrogated interaction with AnkB eliminated RabGAP1L-GFP and AnkB-mCherry vesicular co-localization and co-transport.
source: Furthermore, the KK783EE RabGAP1L-GFP mutant that abrogated interaction with AnkB also eliminated RabGAP1L-GFP and AnkB-mCherry vesicular co-localization and co-transport (Figure 2F center, 2 hr and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse video microscopy showing that the KK783EE mutation disrupts co-localization and co-transport.

claim: Over 60% of RabGAP1L-mCherry vesicles detected in WT MEFs were associated with PI3P-positive vesicles.
source: While over 60% of RabGAP1L-mCherry vesicles detected in WT MEFs were associated with PI3P-positive vesicles, strikingly, less than 20% of RabGAP1L-mCherry localized to PI3P-positive compartments in Ank2-/-MEFs (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data from live microscopy experiments.

claim: Less than 20% of RabGAP1L-mCherry localized to PI3P-positive compartments in Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: While over 60% of RabGAP1L-mCherry vesicles detected in WT MEFs were associated with PI3P-positive vesicles, strikingly, less than 20% of RabGAP1L-mCherry localized to PI3P-positive compartments in Ank2-/-MEFs (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: AnkB recruits RabGAP1L to PI3P-positive organelles.
source: Together, these results reveal a new protein-protein interaction between AnkB and RabGAP1L that recruits RabGAP1L to PI3P-positive organelles.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing AnkB-dependent localization of RabGAP1L to PI3P-positive compartments.

claim: Rab22A is a vertebrate Rab GTPase closely related to Rab5 that localizes to early endosomes.
source: Rab22A is a vertebrate Rab GTPase closely related to Rab5 that localizes to early endosomes, where it interacts with the early endosomal antigen 1 (EEA1) and the Rab5 guanine nucleotide exchange factor Rabex-5 (Kauppi et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature characterizing Rab22A.

claim: Rab22A facilitates the formation of a specialized subset of early endosomes, implicated in endocytosis as well as recycling of both clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent cargos.
source: Interestingly, Rab22A facilitates the formation of a specialized subset of early endosomes, implicated in endocytosis as well as recycling of both clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent cargos (Holloway et al., 2013; Maldonado-Báez and Donaldson, 2013; Weigert et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature describing Rab22A function.

claim: In WT MEFs 40% to 60% of GFP-Rab22A-positive vesicles co-localized with RabGAP1L-mCherry.
source: While in WT MEFs 40% to 60% of GFP-Rab22A-positive vesicles co-localized with RabGAP1L-mCherry, this co-localization was reduced to less than 15% in Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 3B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data from live microscopy experiments.

claim: Co-localization of RabGAP1L with Rab22A was reduced to less than 15% in Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: While in WT MEFs 40% to 60% of GFP-Rab22A-positive vesicles co-localized with RabGAP1L-mCherry, this co-localization was reduced to less than 15% in Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 3B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: In WT MEFs over 40% of Rab22A localized to PI3P-enriched membranes.
source: In line with previous reports of Rab22A association with early endosomes (Kauppi et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2009), we found that in WT MEFs over 40% of Rab22A localized to PI3P-enriched membranes (Figure 3C,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data, with citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of AnkB expression resulted in an increased association of Rab22A with PI3P-positive compartments, especially within the perinuclear region.
source: Remarkably, loss of AnkB expression not only abrogated co-localization of RabGAP1L to Rab22A-positive organelles (Figure 3B,E), but also resulted in an increased association of Rab22A with PI3P-positive compartments, especially within the perinuclear region (Figure 3C,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative co-localization data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: AnkB promotes dissociation of Rab22A from PI3P-enriched organelles through the recruitment of RabGAP1L.
source: Thus, our data indicate that AnkB promotes dissociation of Rab22A from PI3P-enriched organelles through the recruitment of RabGAP1L.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from experiments showing AnkB-dependent recruitment of RabGAP1L and its effect on Rab22A localization.

claim: Photoconverted red WT AnkB vesicles exited the perinuclear region at twice the rate of mutant E1537K AnkB.
source: However, photoconverted red WT AnkB vesicles exited the perinuclear region at twice the rate of mutant E1537K AnkB (Figure 4C,H–I, red symbols).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of photoconversion experiments tracking vesicle movement.

claim: Photoconverted perinuclear WT AnkB-mMaple3 red vesicles exhibited a biased transport toward the migrating front of the cell.
source: Moreover, photoconverted perinuclear WT AnkB-mMaple3 red vesicles exhibited a biased transport toward the migrating front of the cell (Figure 4J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of photoconversion experiments showing directional bias.

claim: Red-converted E1537K AnkB-mMaple3 moved from the perinuclear region into both the front and the rear of cells at equivalent rates.
source: In contrast, red-converted E1537K AnkB-mMaple3 moved from the perinuclear region into both the front and the rear of cells at equivalent rates (Figure 4J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of photoconversion experiments showing loss of directional bias in the mutant.

claim: AnkB, via interaction with RabGAP1L, coordinates the polarized transport of perinuclear PI3P-positive organelles to the migrating front of MEFs.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that AnkB, via interaction with RabGAP1L, coordinates the polarized transport of perinuclear PI3P-positive organelles to the migrating front of MEFs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from photoconversion experiments showing RabGAP1L-dependent polarized transport.

claim: AnkB deficiency did not cause global changes in either plasma membrane protein internalization or recycling.
source: Using a cell surface protein biotinylation assay (Bitsikas et al., 2014), we found that AnkB deficiency did not cause global changes in either plasma membrane protein internalization or recycling, as shown by the similar rate and extent of internalization and recycling of biotinylated surface proteins to the plasma membrane in WT and Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell surface protein biotinylation assay data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: No difference between WT and Ank2-/- MEFs was found in the dynamics of internalization and recycling of transferrin and αvβ3-integrin.
source: We also found no difference between WT and Ank2-/- MEFs in the dynamics of internalization and recycling of known specialized endocytic cargos, including transferrin (Trn) and αvβ3-integrin (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from recycling assays for specific cargos.

claim: In WT MEFs, photoconverted perinuclear α5-integrin-mMaple3 localized to vesicles that were predominantly transported towards the migrating cell front.
source: In WT MEFs, photoconverted perinuclear α5-integrin-mMaple3 localized to vesicles that were predominantly transported towards the migrating cell front (Figure 5A–B and G–I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by photoconversion experiments tracking α5-integrin movement in WT MEFs.

claim: In Ank2-/- MEFs, significantly fewer photoconverted perinuclear α5-integrin-mMaple3 exited the converted region, and showed no preference in transport directionality.
source: In contrast, in Ank2-/- MEFs, significantly fewer photoconverted perinuclear α5-integrin-mMaple3 exited the converted region, and showed no preference in transport directionality (Figure 5C–D and G–I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by photoconversion experiments comparing α5-integrin movement in Ank2-/- MEFs to WT.

claim: AnkB is required for the polarized transport of α5-integrin from the perinuclear region to the migrating front of MEFs.
source: Thus, these results indicate that AnkB is required for the polarized transport of α5-integrin from the perinuclear region to the migrating front of MEFs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from photoconversion experiments showing AnkB-dependent polarized transport of α5-integrin.

claim: After 60 min, WT MEFs recycled over 60% of internalized β1-integrins to the plasma membrane.
source: After 60 min, WT MEFs recycled over 60% of internalized β1-integrins to the plasma membrane (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from β1-integrin recycling assays.

claim: In Ank2-/- MEFs less than 20% of internalized β1-integrins recycled to the cell surface over 60 min, and instead accumulated at the perinuclear region.
source: In contrast, in Ank2-/- MEFs less than 20% of internalized β1-integrins recycled to the cell surface over the same period, and instead accumulated at the perinuclear region (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from β1-integrin recycling assays comparing Ank2-/- to WT MEFs.

claim: Expression of WT AnkB-mCherry fully restored the rate and extent of β1-integrin recycling to the leading edge of migrating Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: Expression of WT AnkB-mCherry fully restored the rate and extent of β1-integrin recycling to the leading edge of migrating Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing restoration of β1-integrin recycling with WT AnkB expression.

claim: Neither E1537K AnkB-mCherry (lacking RabGAP1L binding) nor R1194A AnkB-mCherry (lacking PI3P binding) rescued β1-integrin recycling deficits in Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: In marked contrast, neither E1537K AnkB-mCherry (lacking RabGAP1L binding) nor R1194A AnkB-mCherry (lacking PI3P binding) rescued β1-integrin recycling deficits in Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 6C,D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that specific mutations prevent restoration of β1-integrin recycling.

claim: DD1320AA AnkB-mCherry (unable to bind dynactin) partially rescued β1-integrin recycling to about 50% of the WT levels.
source: DD1320AA AnkB-mCherry (unable to bind dynactin) (Figure 6C) partially rescued β1-integrin recycling to about 50% of the WT levels (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing partial restoration of β1-integrin recycling with the dynactin-binding mutant.

claim: AnkB's binding to PI3P lipids and RabGAP1L are essential steps in β1-integrin recycling, while its association with the dynactin complex increases its efficiency.
source: These results indicate that AnkB's binding to PI3P lipids and RabGAP1L are essential steps in β1-integrin recycling, while its association with the dynactin complex increases its efficiency.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from structure-function rescue experiments testing different AnkB mutants.

claim: Expression of a truncated AnkB-mCherry construct lacking the MBD (Zu5-Ct AnkB-mCherry) was sufficient to restore β1-integrin recycling to the leading edge of Ank2-/- MEFs.
source: To our surprise, expression of a truncated AnkB-mCherry construct lacking the MBD (Zu5-Ct AnkB-mCherry) was sufficient to restore β1-integrin recycling to the leading edge of Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 6C,D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that the MBD is not required for β1-integrin recycling.

claim: Integrin recognition through ANK repeats is not required for AnkB-dependent β1-integrin recycling.
source: Based on these findings, we concluded that integrin recognition through ANK repeats is not required for AnkB-dependent β1-integrin recycling.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the finding that truncated AnkB lacking the MBD can rescue β1-integrin recycling.

claim: The initial sorting of β1-integrin to early endosomes is independent of AnkB.
source: The localization of internalized β1-integrin to Rab22A- or Rab5-positive early endosomes, both in WT and Ank2-/- MEFs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–E), suggests that the initial sorting to early endosomes is independent of AnkB.
evidence: The claim is inferred from co-localization data showing β1-integrin reaches early endosomes in both WT and Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: β1-integrin exhibited increased co-localization with Rab5-positive early endosomes and with Rab22A in Ank2-/- MEFs following initiation of recycling.
source: However, β1-integrin exhibited increased co-localization with Rab5-positive early endosomes and with Rab22A in Ank2-/- MEFs following initiation of recycling (Figure 6E,F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data comparing WT and Ank2-/- MEFs during recycling.

claim: AnkB, through recruitment of RabGAP1L, facilitates the dissociation of Rab22A from β1-integrin-containing endocytic vesicles to allow their transition from Rab5-positive early endosomes to Rab5-negative recycling endosomal compartments.
source: These results indicate that AnkB, through recruitment of RabGAP1L, facilitates the dissociation of Rab22A from β1-integrin-containing endocytic vesicles to allow their transition from Rab5-positive early endosomes to Rab5-negative recycling endosomal compartments.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from co-localization data showing AnkB-dependent effects on Rab22A and Rab5 association with β1-integrin vesicles.

claim: WT MEFs over-expressing WT Rab22A showed a reduced rate of β1-integrin recycling.
source: Interestingly, WT MEFs over-expressing WT Rab22A showed a reduced rate of β1-integrin recycling. The deficiency was further increased in MEFs expressing Q64L Rab22A (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by β1-integrin recycling assays in MEFs overexpressing Rab22A.

claim: The deficiency in β1-integrin recycling was further increased in MEFs expressing Q64L Rab22A.
source: Interestingly, WT MEFs over-expressing WT Rab22A showed a reduced rate of β1-integrin recycling. The deficiency was further increased in MEFs expressing Q64L Rab22A (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by β1-integrin recycling assays comparing WT and constitutively active Rab22A.

claim: WT MEFs expressing Q64L Rab22A affected internalization of β1-integrins, transferrin, and β3-integrins.
source: Moreover, we noticed that WT MEFs expressing Q64L Rab22A not only affected internalization of β1-integrins, but also of transferrin and β3-integrins, whose recycling is not affected in the loss of ankB (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by internalization assays showing broad effects of constitutively active Rab22A.

claim: Hyper-activation of Rab22A disrupts general recycling of multiple receptors while the AnkB-RabGAP1L mediated regulation specifically tunes the Rab22A activity on selected PI3P-positive organelles bearing β1-integrin.
source: These results suggest that hyper-activation of Rab22A disrupts general recycling of multiple receptors while the AnkB-RabGAP1L mediated regulation specifically tunes the Rab22A activity on selected PI3P-positive organelles bearing β1-integrin.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from experiments showing differential effects of Rab22A overexpression versus AnkB loss.

claim: WT MEFs exhibited haptotaxis towards higher concentrations of fibronectin.
source: While WT MEFs, similar to control IA32 fibroblasts, exhibited haptotaxis towards higher concentrations of fibronectin, Ank2-/- MEFs migrated in a random pattern (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by haptotaxis assay data showing directional migration of WT MEFs on fibronectin gradients.

claim: Ank2-/- MEFs migrated in a random pattern on fibronectin gradients.
source: While WT MEFs, similar to control IA32 fibroblasts, exhibited haptotaxis towards higher concentrations of fibronectin, Ank2-/- MEFs migrated in a random pattern (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by haptotaxis assay data showing loss of directional migration in Ank2-/- MEFs.

claim: Ank2-/- MEFs exhibited no difference in the overall velocity or persistence of the cell migration.
source: Interestingly, Ank2-/- MEFs exhibited no difference in the overall velocity or persistence of the cell migration, suggesting that the cell motility machinery is fully functional in the absence of AnkB (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of migration velocity and persistence in haptotaxis assays.

claim: Expression of WT AnkB-GFP restored the haptotatic migration pattern in Ank2-/- MEFs while E1537K AnkB-GFP did not rescue the impaired haptotactic response.
source: Interestingly, rescue experiments in Ank2-/- MEFs expressing either WT or E1537K AnkB-GFP (lacking RabGAP1L binding) showed that expression of WT AnkB-GFP restored the haptotatic migration pattern in Ank2-/- MEFs while E1537K AnkB-GFP did not rescue the impaired haptotactic response (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing RabGAP1L-binding-dependent restoration of haptotaxis.

claim: The AnkB-RabGAP1L interaction, which is required for polarized recycling of β1-integrin, is also required for efficient fibroblast migration along a fibronectin gradient.
source: Together, these data indicate that the AnkB-RabGAP1L interaction, which is required for polarized recycling of β1-integrin, is also required for efficient fibroblast migration along a fibronectin gradient.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from haptotaxis experiments showing that the AnkB-RabGAP1L interaction is necessary for directional migration.

claim: AnkB functions as a PI3P effector associated with early endosomes in fibroblasts.
source: We demonstrate that in fibroblasts AnkB functions as a PI3P effector associated with early endosomes, and describe a new interaction of AnkB with RabGAP1L.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement supported by multiple experiments showing AnkB's PI3P-dependent localization to early endosomes.

claim: AnkB recruits RabGAP1L to PI3P-positive organelles, where it inactivates Rab22A.
source: Moreover, we show that AnkB recruits RabGAP1L to PI3P-positive organelles, where it inactivates Rab22A
evidence: The claim is a summary statement supported by co-localization and functional experiments.

claim: α5β1-integrin is a specialized cargo that depends on AnkB/RabGAP1L for efficient recycling to the leading edge of migrating fibroblasts.
source: and identify α5β1-integrin as a specialized cargo that depends on AnkB/RabGAP1L for efficient recycling to the leading edge of migrating fibroblasts (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is a summary statement supported by photoconversion and recycling experiments.

claim: AnkB is a key nodal element in the protein circuitry required for α5β1-integrin recycling and for directional fibroblast migration on fibronectin gradients.
source: Thus, our results establish AnkB as a key nodal element in the protein circuitry required for α5β1-integrin recycling and for directional fibroblast migration on fibronectin gradients.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing AnkB's role in integrin recycling and haptotaxis.

claim: Human AnkB, RabGAP1L, and Rab22A all have homologues in ghost sharks and zebrafish with a high level of sequence similarity, including nearly complete conservation of their AnkB-RabGAP1L binding sites.
source: Human AnkB, RabGAP1L, and Rab22A all have homologues in ghost sharks and zebrafish with a high level of sequence similarity, including nearly complete conservation of their AnkB-RabGAP1L binding sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis showing conservation across vertebrate species.

claim: Residues required for interaction between AnkB and RabGAP1L are highly divergent in the closest homologues of Drosophila melanogaster and C. elegans.
source: In contrast, residues required for interaction between AnkB and RabGAP1L are highly divergent in the closest homologues of Drosophila melanogaster and C. elegans.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis showing divergence in invertebrate homologues.

claim: AnkB likely gained RabGAP1L-binding activity after divergence of AnkB and AnkG proteins in early vertebrate evolution.
source: AnkB, likely gained RabGAP1L-binding activity after divergence of AnkB and AnkG proteins in early vertebrate evolution, although, alternatively, AnkG may have lost this function.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on sequence divergence and binding specificity data.

claim: Rab22A participates in recycling of the Menkes copper transporter, the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and the major histocompatibility complex class I.
source: In support of this idea, Rab22A, an AnkB/RabGAP1L substrate identified in this study, participates in recycling of other specialized cargos, including the Menkes copper transporter, the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and the major histocompatibility complex class I (Holloway et al., 2013; Maldonado-Báez and Donaldson, 2013; Weigert et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature describing Rab22A's role in recycling various cargos.

claim: Rab22A shares 70% sequence identity with Rab22B/Rab31, also implicated in the endosomal transport of specialized cargos such as EGFR and the p75 neurotrophin receptor.
source: Interestingly, Rab22A shares 70% sequence identity with Rab22B/Rab31, also implicated in the endosomal transport of specialized cargos such as EGFR and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (Baeza-Raja et al., 2012; Chua and Tang, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and citations to previous literature on Rab22B/Rab31.

claim: A strong PLA signal was detected in the corpus callosum in the CNS and costameres in skeletal muscle.
source: We detected a strong PLA signal in the corpus callosum in the CNS and costameres in skeletal muscle (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by proximity ligation assay data in brain and skeletal muscle tissues.

claim: AnkB is required for preservation of the corpus callosum and assembly of costameres.
source: Interestingly, AnkB is required for preservation of the corpus callosum and assembly of costameres (Scotland et al., 1998; Lorenzo et al., 2014; Ayalon et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature describing AnkB's role in these structures.

claim: GTP-bound Rab22A directly associates with the Rab5 GEF Rabex-1, which activates Rab5.
source: GTP-bound Rab22A directly associates with the Rab5 GEF Rabex-1, which activates Rab5 (Zhu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature describing the Rab22A-Rabex-1 interaction.

claim: Conversion of Rab22A to its GDP form through the AnkB-mediated recruitment of RabGAP1L would be expected to reduce Rab5 activation, thus promoting loss of early endosome identity.
source: Alternatively, conversion of Rab22A to its GDP form through the AnkB-mediated recruitment of RabGAP1L would be expected to reduce Rab5 activation, thus promoting loss of early endosome identity.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference based on known interactions between Rab22A and Rab5 activation.

claim: Diacylglycerol kinase α (DGKα) is required for Rab-coupling protein (RCP)-dependent integrin trafficking.
source: Specifically, previous studies had shown that Diacylglycerol kinase α (DGKα) is required for Rab-coupling protein (RCP)-dependent integrin trafficking and Akt mediated phosphorylation of ACAP1, a GAP for Afr6, is required for integrin recycling (Rainero et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature on kinase regulation of integrin trafficking.

claim: Akt mediated phosphorylation of ACAP1, a GAP for Afr6, is required for integrin recycling.
source: Specifically, previous studies had shown that Diacylglycerol kinase α (DGKα) is required for Rab-coupling protein (RCP)-dependent integrin trafficking and Akt mediated phosphorylation of ACAP1, a GAP for Afr6, is required for integrin recycling (Rainero et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature on kinase regulation of integrin recycling.

claim: Rab22A contributes to exosome biogenesis and shedding from primary tumor cells and tumor metastasis.
source: Interestingly, Rab22A also contributes to exosome biogenesis and shedding from primary tumor cells and tumor metastasis (Wang et al., 2014b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature on Rab22A's role in cancer.

claim: Long-range transport and targeting of integrins underlies neurite outgrowth and neuronal migration.
source: Long-range transport and targeting of integrins underlies neurite outgrowth and neuronal migration (Anton et al., 1999; Condic, 2001; Condic and Letourneau, 1997; Wu and Reddy, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature on integrin function in neurons.

claim: Proper levels and dynamics of α5β1-integrin complexes are required in multiple stages of brain development and synaptic function.
source: Moreover, proper levels and dynamics of α5β1-integrin complexes, shown to localize to nerve growth cones, are required in multiple stages of brain development and synaptic function (Bi et al., 2001; Graus-Porta et al., 2001; Marchetti et al., 2010; Yanagida et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature on integrin function in brain development.

claim: The neuron-specific 440 kDa AnkB isoform is exclusively targeted to axons and enriched at axonal growth cones.
source: Intriguingly, the neuron-specific 440 kDa AnkB isoform is exclusively targeted to axons and enriched at axonal growth cones and might play a role in axonal guidance (Kunimoto, 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature on the 440 kDa AnkB isoform localization.

claim: An AnkB/RabGAP1L pathway might facilitate the 440 kDa AnkB-mediated axonal growth cone behavior, axonal guidance and synaptogenesis.
source: It is, thus, conceivable that similar to its roles in migrating fibroblasts, an AnkB/RabGAP1L pathway might facilitate the 440 kDa AnkB-mediated axonal growth cone behavior, axonal guidance and synaptogenesis.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the role of AnkB/RabGAP1L in fibroblasts and the localization of 440 kDa AnkB in neurons.
